rv.q: For fans of this score, and there are many of us enthusiasts, this staging is very rewarding.

In staging the production in the intimate 165-seat Copley Theatre, director Jim Corti has shaped an emotionally rich, electrifying and ultimately uplifting meditation on love, loss and the often cruelly fickle nature of recovery.
All of these actors are just as perfect as the show is.
Mr. Corti’s production is beautifully nuanced and simply extraordinary.
Paramount Theatre’s Bold Series summer production of acclaimed musical Next to Normal is hauntingly, disturbingly, emotionally brilliant.

Artfully written, with wry humor and a rock-infused score punctuated by power chords and wailing guitars, the Pulitzer Prize-winning show is a wrenching examination of loss and grief, bipolar disorder and the efforts of a damaged family to repair itself.

Though Next To Normal might not be for those who want a lighter subject matter, if you're a fan of modern musicals diving into the twists and turns of a family delivered through top notch singing (in this writer's opinion), this would be a good fit for you.
This show has a kickass rock opera essence to it that goes beyond the themes, the music, and the story to create the biggest of feels.
If you have never seen "Next to Normal", and want to see one of the best productions, ever, I suggest you get to it right away as you only have a month.

cn.t: Critics praise this "hauntingly brilliant" production for its unflinching, compassionate portrayal of mental illness, elevated by extraordinary performances and Tom Kitt's gorgeous rock-infused score, though the heavy subject matter isn't for everyone.
